family.tagline: Two parents, two children and one Companion Core on the living room mantel.
family.story: Marisol manages a clinic office and Andres works in devops. Camila, ten, and Mateo, seven, each have a room upstairs. One Companion Core on the living room mantel serves all four.

companion.name: Willow
companion.job: Drafts Marisol’s replies to the school and the swim club from her notes.
companion.limits: Drafts only. Marisol reads every message and sends it herself.

companion.name: Thimble
companion.job: Drafts Andres’s weekly change notes for the family from his short messages.
companion.limits: Drafts only. Andres reads each note and sends it himself.

popup.title: A parcel on the front step
popup.body: A parcel waits on the front step. Andres carries the Companion Core through the foyer to the living room.

popup.title: Unbox the Companion Core
popup.body: Inside: the Companion Core, a power cable, a quick-start guide and a recovery USB drive. Marisol lifts the Core out and sets it on the mantel.

popup.title: Plug it in
popup.body: Andres plugs in the cable and Mateo presses the button. The Core wakes and opens its own Wi-Fi network.

popup.title: Join it from a phone
popup.body: Marisol opens the Wi-Fi settings on her phone and joins the Core’s own network. Then she chooses the home network.

popup.title: Pick the first agent and apps
popup.body: In the Companion Hub store, Marisol picks Hermes, and the family adds Yuvomi and Linkwarden. Then they walk away.

beats.capability: an agent that connects to chat apps, email and more from one self-hosted app

popup.title: Willow says hello
popup.body: Marisol messages Willow, the agent she named. Willow answers from the Core on the mantel beside her.
popup.note: Messages pass through the chat service you choose.

say.speaker: marisol
say.text: Good morning. I am Willow. What shall we start with?

beats.capability: plan tasks and time blocks in one local file on your Core

popup.title: Marisol blocks out her shifts
popup.body: On Saturday morning, from the chesterfield, Marisol blocks out her clinic shifts. Companion Planning keeps the time blocks in one local file on the Core.

beats.capability: stream your own movies, shows and music to every screen in the house

popup.title: Hers before lunch, his after
popup.body: Camila and Mateo take turns choosing: hers before lunch, his after. Jellyfin plays both from the family’s own files on the Core to the family room TV.

beats.capability: a family planner with a shared calendar, tasks, shopping, meals

popup.title: Basil goes on the shopping list
popup.body: The herb pots by the window need basil, so Andres adds it to the shopping list in Yuvomi. The family shares that list, and its data sits on the Core.

beats.capability: a family planner with a shared calendar, tasks, shopping, meals

popup.title: The fee moves off the fridge
popup.body: A recorder-lesson fee is due on Friday, pinned to the fridge by a magnet. Marisol enters it in the budget in Yuvomi, and the figures sit on the Core.

beats.capability: scan and file your paperwork; it reads every page, tags it and makes it searchable

popup.title: Marisol clears the table of forms
popup.body: School forms and bills crowd the farmhouse table. Marisol scans each one into Paperless-ngx on the Core, where every page is read and tagged.

beats.capability: an agent that connects to chat apps, email and more from one self-hosted app

popup.title: Three lines become a family note
popup.body: Andres types three scrappy lines to Thimble about what changed on the Core. Thimble turns them into a note Marisol can read, and Andres edits it and sends it himself.
popup.note: Messages pass through the chat service you choose.

say.speaker: andres
say.text: Plain version is here. Cut whatever reads like a pipeline.

beats.capability: store every password in a vault you host; works with the Bitwarden apps

popup.title: Where the library password lives
popup.body: A password service would have held the school, library and swim club passwords. Marisol keeps them in one VaultWarden vault on the Core. VaultWarden works with the Bitwarden apps.

beats.capability: an agent that connects to chat apps, email and more from one self-hosted app

popup.title: A missed swim lesson, explained
popup.body: Marisol messages Willow about a missed swim lesson. Willow drafts the note to the coach on the Core’s local model. Marisol reads it and sends it herself.
popup.note: Messages pass through the chat service you choose.

say.speaker: marisol
say.text: Draft is ready, Marisol. Read it and change what you like.

beats.capability: save web pages with a screenshot and a PDF so they survive link rot

popup.title: Camila tags her bee pages
popup.body: For her bee project, Camila saves pages into a Linkwarden collection, tagged hive, queen or flowers. Linkwarden keeps each page on the Core, with a PDF copy beside it.

beats.capability: translate text and documents on your own Core

popup.title: Camila reads the newsletter aloud
popup.body: Grandmother reads Spanish, and the school newsletter is in English. Camila pastes one paragraph into LibreTranslate, which translates on the Core, and reads it out. Its models were downloaded once.

beats.capability: the Obsidian note app in your browser; notes stay as local Markdown files

popup.title: Camila maps the moon’s phases
popup.body: After school, Camila draws the moon’s phases in her Obsidian notes and labels each one. The notes are plain Markdown files on the Core.

beats.capability: find photos by face, object and place, with albums built by date and location

popup.title: Mateo finishes a dragon
popup.body: At his easel, Mateo finishes a dragon, and Marisol photographs it. LibrePhotos builds albums by date on the Core, not in a photo cloud.

beats.capability: model low-poly 3D art and Minecraft-style models in your browser

popup.title: One dragon, built twice
popup.body: On the floor cushion by the toy box, Mateo rebuilds the dragon in Blockbench, block by block. The Core serves the editor, and he saves the model himself.

beats.capability: host your own git repositories, issues and pull requests on your Core

popup.title: The house scripts get a repository
popup.body: A devops engineer, Andres gives the house scripts a repository of their own. Forgejo keeps it, with its issues, on the Core, not on a rented code host.

beats.capability: watch your sites and services and get an alert when one goes down

popup.title: Andres watches the house’s apps
popup.body: On Sunday afternoon, Andres points Uptime Kuma at the family’s apps, and the checks run on the Core. When one stops answering, he gets an alert.

beats.capability: block ads, trackers and bad domains for devices on your network at the DNS level

popup.title: Andres changes who the TV asks
popup.body: In the den, Andres sets the TV to ask the Core for DNS. Pi-hole then blocks ad and tracker domains for it, and for any device that uses it.

beats.capability: track your plants, watering and care history, with photos and a garden journal

popup.title: Whose row of beans is winning?
popup.body: Each child planted a row of beans in the garden beds. Camila logs the sprouts in HortusFox, a journal on the Core, while Mateo insists his row is winning.

popup.title: One Core, a busy house
popup.body: Forms, photos, code and one dragon live on a Companion Core, on the living room mantel.

closing.body: Your family’s forms, photos, repositories and homework can live on a Companion Core at home. Browse the Companion Hub store and choose your first apps.

notes: The Den has a sofa, an ottoman and nesting tables but no desk: Andres works from the sofa. His den beats anchor on the Den sofa and the Den TV, with room office as the tail; his Thimble beat sits at the dining table.
The living chapter spans the Living Room (couch beat, chesterfield is couch nth 2 in living) and the Family Room (tv nth 0, tv-stand); the Den TV (wall-tv) is used only in den-dns.

Mateo (maker) has Jellyfin as his persona-pool app in living-film. LibrePhotos and Blockbench are signature apps outside the maker pool. Blockbench is a static web build: the beat says he saves the model himself.
No code-server, Calibre-Web, Ollama, Open WebUI or Mealie: none needs a reviewed.json entry. Open WebUI was dropped from camila-moon to keep the fleet under its app cap.

Hermes beats carry the chat-service note. Pi-hole is told as one household instance for devices that use it for DNS. No Companion Memory is named. Companion Planning is told as Marisol's own planner; Yuvomi carries the household planning.
Kids rooms: room kids nth 0 is the Kids Room (desk, single bed), nth 1 the Kids Bedroom (easel, house bed, toy box). Nobody is shown asleep.
The hero Core sits at the fireplace mantel in the Living Room, so the copy says mantel; casting's coreSpot says shelf.
